# ShiftBay → Riverbend Family Health: outreach pack

## 1. Email sequence to Mary Major

### Email 1 — Tuesday 16 September 2025

**Subject:** Your float-pool question from the 3 Sept webinar

Hi Mary,

You asked during our "Fixing last-minute shift gaps" webinar how float-pool nurses fit into automated call-out filling. Here's a fuller answer than I managed live.

In ShiftBay, a float nurse is just another qualified person on the list. When a shift opens at any of your 14 clinics, it goes by app to everyone credentialed and available for it — site staff and floats alike — and the first to accept gets it, unless taking it would push them into overtime. Nobody has to text people one by one.

You also said filling call-outs by text burns hours every week and overtime is your fastest-growing cost. With three new clinics this year, I'd guess both have got harder.

Would you give me 20 minutes to walk me through how your float pool works today? If we're not a fit, I'll say so.

Sam Okafor
Founder, ShiftBay

---

### Email 2 — Thursday 25 September 2025

**Subject:** Overtime: what our six customers actually saw (full range)

Hi Mary,

Following up with numbers, since overtime is the cost you flagged.

Across our six customers, overtime hours fell 18% on average over the first six months. The range is wide: 8% at the low end, 40% at Northfield Clinics (nine sites), where call-outs are now filled in a median of 22 minutes. The group nearest your size, 12 clinics, saw 15%.

I'd rather you plan on something like 15–18% and be pleasantly surprised than hear 40% from me and be disappointed. Northfield's result is also better explained by them than by me.

One caveat: at 14 clinics you'd be our largest customer. Northfield and Pinegate Health have both agreed to take reference calls, so you can ask about the rollout as well as the results.

Would a 30-minute call with Northfield be useful? I can arrange it for next week.

Sam

---

### Email 3 — Tuesday 7 October 2025

**Subject:** No deadline from me — but here's your real one

Hi Mary,

Your contract renews on 30 November 2026 with 90 days' notice, so your real decision point is around 1 September 2026 (do check the contract). Nothing has to happen this quarter, and I won't invent a deadline.

The reason to look now: every month call-outs are filled by text is another month of the overtime you called your fastest-growing cost, and with eleven RN roles open, that won't ease on its own.

Implementation takes about six weeks and we import from your current tool's export, so starting with one or two clinics next year is realistic — long before notice is due.

If you'd like to see it, describe one real call-out from a bad week at your busiest clinic and I'll run that scenario in a 30-minute demo. If it's "not yet", say so and I'll go quiet until spring.

Sam

---

## 2. LinkedIn connection note (≈245 characters)

> Hi Mary — Sam here, founder of ShiftBay. Your float-pool question at our 3 Sept webinar stuck with me; I've emailed you a fuller answer than I managed live. No pitch in this note — just glad to connect with someone running clinical ops across 14 sites.

---

## 3. Note to John

John — thanks for the steer. Here's what I did with it.

**Used**

- **Overtime as the lead theme.** It's her own phrase ("fastest-growing cost"), so every email comes back to it.
- **The ask for a meeting.** Email 1 asks for a 20-minute call rather than a demo, because I don't yet know how her float pool works and a generic demo wastes a VP's time. The demo is the ask in email 3, built around one of her real call-outs.
- **Northfield's 40%.** It's in email 2 — attributed to Northfield, sitting next to the 18% average and the 15% from our 12-clinic customer (unnamed; they haven't cleared it). Riverbend at 14 clinics is bigger than anyone we've served. If I open with 40% and she lands at 15%, she'll feel misled at exactly the moment we want her to renew. A 40% she can verify on a reference call is more convincing than a 40% in a subject line.

**Rejected**

- **30% off.** My discretion ends at 15% for multi-year. Above that needs CFO approval and has never been granted, so I'd be dangling something I can't deliver and would have to retract — worse than never offering. Pricing comes up on the call; if she wants multi-year, 15% is available.
- **"Sign by Friday."** Her renewal is 30 November 2026 with notice due around 1 September 2026 — she has 14 months and she knows it. A Friday deadline reads as a bluff she can call, and it teaches her to wait for the next discount. The real urgency is her overtime bill, which email 3 uses instead. With a six-week implementation, she should ideally decide by mid-2026 so the switch isn't rushed; I'll say that when we're talking.

**Also**

- Only Northfield and Pinegate are named. The other four appear as aggregates.
- I told her she'd be our largest customer. She'll find out on the reference call anyway; better it comes from me.
- Cadence: 16 Sep, 25 Sep, 7 Oct, then silence until March 2026 unless she replies.

Sam
